extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (respondents), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys involved in reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority. Covers notice, response deadlines, service, publication, and the form/content of a Notice of Reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by 'having been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on this page: the State of Michigan issued a public reprimand (approved settlement) predicated upon Respondent's guilty plea to Disorderly Conduct - Persisting (a misdemeanor) arising from a traffic incident and a subsequent threatening letter. The USPTO imposed reciprocal public reprimand based on that state discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the USPTO impose identical discipline to that imposed by a State; a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be mailed to the respondent informing them of the Complaint and proposed reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order was issued pursuant to a Notice and Order (mailed March 4, 2010) requesting a public reprimand identical to that imposed by the State of Michigan. The Notice and Order must advise the respondent of the process to contest imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligation to file a response to contest reciprocal discipline (§ 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, if seeking to contest imposition of public reprimand pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), 'shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the State ... would be unwarranted' based upon grounds permissible under § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed the 40-day deadline and specific content. The respondent here did not file a response; absence of such a response supports a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for determining whether reciprocal discipline is appropriate (§ 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to raise a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d), the USPTO may determine that there is no genuine issue and that imposition of reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On this page the Office determined: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) a public reprimand of Respondent is appropriate. The text ties procedural default (no response) to the finding of appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements (certificate of service and mailing) per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Order must be served; certificate of service shows the Final Order was 'mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested' to the respondent's most recent address provided to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes a Certificate of Service verifying the mailing to the respondent's address and the date (JUN - 3 2010). Use of certified mail with return receipt requested and reliance on the most recent address on file are required practices reflected here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director 'shall publish this Final Order' and 'shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette' and, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, 'shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires posting disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room (link provided) and publication in the Official Gazette; notice to state agencies, courts, and the public is mandated. The page reproduces the Notice of Reprimand text that the OED will publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content/format of a Notice of Reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Reprimand should identify the practitioner (name and registration number), state that the practitioner 'has been publicly reprimanded by the United States Patent and Trademark Office' and specify the regulatory provision violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)), together with a factual summary of the state disciplinary proceeding and the underlying misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice reproduced here provides a model: it names the respondent and registration number, states the violation and basis (public reprimand by State), cites the state case (Attorney Grievance Commission v. James L. Lindon, Case No. 09-37-JC), and briefly summarizes the underlying misdemeanor and facts (traffic incident and threatening letter). This demonstrates the expected factual granularity and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority citation for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, here cited as '35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states these authorities as the basis for the action; including proper citations is part of an administratively valid Final Order.
